title: How New Orleans has changed since he left
summary: They discuss the remaining old district buildings, the new City Hall, Rampart Street, Union Station and street names.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, there's just one little corner there of the old district that's left the place, around the corner where Lula's had a saloon. I guess it was a bar room next to Lula. Yes. That building's still there. I see. And then the one back, a couple little crib places. And then the one at the corner, somebody told me Tony Jackson used to play.
Yes.
There was Franklin and the Edmonds.
Yeah.
That building's still there, everything else is there. Even all the buildings around there. The town has really been chanted.
Yes.
Rampart Street has been in the little neutral ground, the place of being a big garden. They put it down about six feet higher.
Yes, they cut out of trees from it, put you to far left there.
Yeah, cut down all the trees. There was a big highway that goes through where Basin Street is now, up to the City Hall and all that. Have you seen the new City Hall? I guess not.
No, I saw there's simply a postcard of it. It's right there on the Dio.
It's beautiful building. Remember where the Funky Butt Hall used to be?
Yes.
The City Hall sits on all that character. When Louis was raised, all those on Liberty Street, all that just to be vacant lots or else the City Hall and building a big library.
Yeah, they changed that town a lot. Oh, yeah. You saw the Union Station. Transformation.
Well, the rest of the town, they saw them modern life that day.
They had completed landscape in front of it when I left.
They saw them now. They got a big statue up there or somebody.
Is it Clayborne? I don't know.
Either Ivorville or Bienville or somebody. Yeah, it was one of those. I think one of the guys that discovered or founded New Orleans.
Governor Claiborne was, he was governing Russia. There were three brothers on the streets with AMAP, the Claiborne, Bienville, and Ivorville.
Well, I think Claiborne was later. They gave us the first American governor when he came to.
That's right.
That's right. I think Ivorville and Bienville came over in 1700. So, before that, the founder of the city. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Anyway, some of those guys.
They're supposed to have been brothers. I don't know.

Two of them are brothers, I don't know. Well, I can't think of anything else to ask you. I think we've started covering the steel. Of course, I mean, you can talk. I hope someday maybe you can... You still ought to try to get everything together.
